description: The pie chart represents the proportion of correct corrections among various error detection results in a novel detector-corrector framework for Chinese spelling correction. The chart is divided into six slices, each representing a different category of error detection results. The largest slice, accounting for 56% of the total, represents the errors in high precision results, denoted by "P". The second largest slice, representing 29% of the total, corresponds to the errors in high recall results, denoted by "R". The third largest slice, accounting for 26% of the total, represents the errors that were not detected, denoted by "N". The remaining three slices, each representing 1% of the total, correspond to the errors in high precision results with correction failure, denoted by "PW", the errors in high recall results with correction failure, denoted by "RW", and the errors in high precision results with correction failure, denoted by "NW". The chart does not include any visual emphasis on any of the slices, and there is no legend or percentage labels inside the slices. The slices are ordered in descending size, with the largest slice representing the errors in high precision results, followed by the errors in high recall results, and then the errors that were not detected.
